measured.what: Which kinds of edit install in place
measured.unit: edit kinds, plus sampled agent commits
measured.method: 1,437 agent-written Megatron commits were classified by a script as: no code change, installable by a function swap, or needing a restart. 34 commits were then drawn evenly from the restart group and installed into one running process, each followed by a correctness check.
measured.caveat: This is an earlier build of the lab for Megatron, which re-imports changed files. It is not the lab in repos/megatron on main: that one swaps function bodies and refuses constructors, new fields and module-level changes (3 of 6 real upstream PRs were refused). 34 of 34 is not a property of the public repo's Megatron lab.

measured.what: Which mechanism a real performance PR needs
measured.method: 487 performance PRs found (2026-07-24 to 2026-10-24); 80 sampled and inspected by hand (71/80 = 89% install in place in this repo: 63/80 via Python, graph, and resource paths plus 8/80 = 10% C++/CUDA native edits via repos/vllm/livelab/adapter/native.py; 9/80 = 11% restart). A classification of what each PR would need, not a test that each installs.

rows.mechanism: Swap Python methods or objects in place
Swap code inside compiled graphs, recapture graphs, re-JIT kernels
Swap code and rebuild pre-allocated buffers or runners
Compile C++/CUDA into a versioned shared library, recapture (repos/vllm/livelab/adapter/native.py + Library rebind + R1)
Needs a restart (Rust rebuild, weights, startup logic, launch flags)

measured.caveat: Shares are of 80 hand-read PRs, not of code. The class column (live, partial reset, restart) is this page's grouping of the five mechanisms.

measured.what: What v1 actually did with 19 merged upstream PRs
measured.method: Each PR replayed through the lab on GB200 (two models, TP1 and TP2, eager and CUDA graphs).
